lever.name: foveated-read
lever.problem: Lexical minification (strip comments, collapse whitespace) targets the cheap 10-20% of tokens and removes high-density comprehension signal. The expensive waste is boilerplate, repetition, and re-reads.
lever.strategy: Layered retrieval. Read an outline first, raw ranges second, full file only if required. Deduplicate repeated blocks at repo level. Memoize reads by content hash.

protocol.layer: File tree, sizes, content hashes. Once per session.
Exports, signatures, types, line ranges. Bodies collapsed. Repeated blocks replaced with references. ~10-15% of file tokens.
Raw source of named line ranges. Full fidelity. This is what the agent edits.
Raw source. Only when L2 is insufficient.

commands.cmd: outline <path> -> L1 outline with line ranges and refs
read <path> -> L3 raw, with a warning that L1 exists
read-status <path> -> "already read, unchanged" or "changed since turn N"

lever.baseline_command: # Measure current read volume # Sum of file sizes read in the session, in bytes / 4 for token estimate. # Record: total files read, total bytes, re-read count.
lever.verification_command: # After enabling foveated-read, run the same task. # Success: >= 50% reduction in bytes read, zero re-reads of unchanged files, # and the agent edited raw L2 source (not an outline).

safety_gates.gate: Edits always operate on L2/L3 raw source. Never on an outline.
Dedup references must be resolvable. If resolve fails, fall back to raw.
Hash check on every read. Stale memo is a correctness bug, not a nuisance.
If the repo has no AST parser for the language, fall back to L3 raw. Do not fake an outline with regex.
Never dedup across trust boundaries (secrets, keys, credentials). These must remain inline or be redacted, never referenced.

tools.tool: Required for L1 outlines. grammars per language. vix is the reference implementation.

trade_offs.trade: Requires agent cooperation to request ranges.
Dedup breaks naive grep; resolve command required.
Savings compound with repo size and session length — opposite of per-file minification, which is flat.
